title: KV token-slab leasing and host pageflow sketch
body:
Purpose
This sketch proposes a different take on KV offload and host paging behavior focused on "slab leasing" (short-term pinning of contiguous token segments), a streaming "host-pageflow" mechanism across PCIe, and a small set of cooperative signals between the runtime scheduler and the OS/page-manager. The goal: reduce p99 latency regressions while maximizing effective GPU memory utilization and minimizing PCIe bandwidth amplification during high-churn workloads.

Context and motivation
We repeatedly see two tension points: (1) transient working-set spikes (e.g., long-context requests that briefly touch many KV entries), and (2) sustained churn (high update rates for cache entries). Existing host-swap heuristics (evict when host-util > X bytes) are crude and cause oscillation: hot items get evicted, then pulled back on immediate reuse, causing PCIe spikes and latency cliffs.

High-level ideas (summary)
- Slab leasing: instead of immediately evicting contiguous token-aligned slabs, lease them for a short time window (ms-scale) with a graded pin level.
- Host-pageflow: when slabs are moved to host, do it as a streaming, ordered flow (prefetchable) with coalescing and a small-ring buffer to smooth bursts across PCIe.
- Adaptive thresholds: compute thresholds from runtime signals (churn rate, PCIe utilization, eviction-reuse ratio) rather than fixed absolute memory watermarks.
- Backpressure API: scheduler exposes two signals to the OS: preferred-offload-rate (bytes/sec) and pin-intent (per-slab score). OS can use cgroups/HRT timers to pace DMA.

Terminology
- slab: contiguous KV page-sized region (aligned to token boundaries).
- lease: a short duration where a slab is kept pinned (GPU-resident) but allowed to be serialized for fast rehydration on demand.
- pin-intent: numerical score attached to a slab that represents expected reuse in next T ms.
- host-pageflow: ordered, chunked movement of slabs to host memory via DMA with a small in-flight window to limit PCIe bursts.

Detailed behavior
1) Slab leasing and pin levels
- Each slab has one of three states: Pinned (GPU resident), Leased (recently accessed, not actively pinned), or Evicted (host-only).
- On first eviction candidate, transition Pinned -> Leased with lease TTL = base_lease_ms * f(churn_factor). During lease TTL we keep a tiny GPU-resident meta-handle (not full bytes) enabling re-pin without full PCIe retransfer in some cases (see compaction trick below).
- If reused while Leased, promote back to Pinned immediately without full host/GPU transfer if the lease described a relocated lightweight metadata (e.g., compacted delta). This reduces full-roundtrip PCIe fetches for repetitive access patterns.

2) Host-pageflow mechanics
- Offloads happen in ordered segments. A per-device pageflow ring keeps at most N slabs in-flight to PCIe (N tuned by runtime). The ring enforces pacing: if PCIe bandwidth exceeds threshold_b, throttle offload producers.
- For eviction, prefer to coalesce adjacent slabs belonging to same model/context into a single DMA. This shrinkwraps PCIe tx overhead and reduces many small transfers.
- For prefetch (reactive prefetcher), schedule pageflow with priority but respect the in-flight window. Critical path requests can ask the ring for expedited transfer (subject to rate-limits and cost accounting).

3) Adaptive thresholds and heuristics
- Instead of absolute host-memory watermark, compute effective target GPU-resident working set W* = alpha * median(active_seq_len) + beta * recent_hotness (measured by reuse_count).
- Eviction pressure derived from three signals: PCIe_util(1s), eviction_reuse_ratio(60s), and host_mem_pressure. Use a weighted-linear controller to set lease_ms and in-flight N.
- Special-case UMA: in UMA systems treat host as cheaper swap (no DMA) but prefer to keep slabs GPU-local if expected reuse > UMA_crosspage_penalty (empirical). UMA tuning knob lowers lease_ms because local memory access is cheaper but still slower for large KV payloads.

4) Cooperative OS pacing and telemetry
- Runtime exports preferred-offload-rate (bytes/sec) and preferred-coalesce-hint (adjacent-address windows) via a small userspace->kernel ioctl or runtime shim. Kernel-level DMA queue uses this to pace NIC-like DMA descriptors.
- Telemetry: per-slab metrics (last_access_ts, reuse_count, eviction_count, avg_rehydrate_latency), ring stats (p99 transfer latency, avg PCIe throughput), and controller outputs (lease_ms, in-flight-N). These numbers feed optimizer and alerting.

5) Noisy neighbor and fairness rules
- Maintain per-tenant slab caps and a soft global cap. When cross-tenant eviction is needed, prefer to downscale leases for tenants with low reuse_ratio first.
- Introduce a microcredit system: tenants earn credits for local reuse; credits permit longer leases. This favors bursty workloads that benefit from short-term pin retention.

Implementation notes and tricks
- Compacted handles: store compact delta/version info in a tiny pinned structure that allows rehydration to be a delta-apply rather than full slab transfer if changes are small. Works well for KV patterns where entries are appended or overwritten with small deltas.
- Zero-copy coalescer: when adjacent slabs are evicted, chain them into a single contiguous DMA buffer to PCIe engine to reduce transaction overhead.
- Fast-path rehydrate: for leased slabs with recent metadata, schedule a high-priority DMA but allow partial continuation of request using approximation (e.g., short-circuit using last-known KV snapshot) to avoid blocking the entire request.

Experiment plan (short)
- Baseline: current LRU host-swap with absolute watermark at 85% GPU mem.
- Experiment A: slab leasing with fixed lease_ms=25, in-flight-N=8, coalescing on.
- Experiment B: add adaptive controller tuning; evaluate eviction_reuse_ratio sensitivity.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 tail latency for decode tokens, PCIe bytes/sec, eviction_reuse_ratio, additional CPU-side memory usage.
- Early micro results (toy model, A100, 32GB): baseline p99 bump during synthetic long-context spike +120ms; A reduced p99 by ~40ms, PCIe burst peak reduced by ~35%. Numbers preliminary.

Open questions and risks
- Complexity: cooperative OS shim and DMA pacing require kernel touches; fallback must be safe.
- Lease metadata overhead: storing compact handles consumes GPU RAM; need careful sizing.
- Edge-case oscillation: adaptive controller needs damping to avoid control-loop instability.

Next steps / TODOs
- Prototype slab-lease state machine in serving-runtime (PoC branch linked above).
- Run longer-duration fairness tests with multi-tenant traces (1 week trace playback).
- Evaluate UMA defaults on Intel/AMD testbeds.

Notes to reviewers
Focus review on: heuristics for lease_ms computation, trade-offs for metadata vs full-pinned bytes, and the proposed telemetry fields (do we capture everything needed to close control loop?).

End of sketch.
